sections.title: Pharmaceutical quality system
sections.text: The pharmaceutical quality system (PQS) principles were adequately described in the Quality Manual. A documented system for quality assurance (QA) at the corporate level was established, with procedures covering key quality elements. The quality department, including QA and QC, was separate from the production department. Operations were documented in writing, and critical GMP requirements were essentially met. The procedures reviewed and discussed during the inspection were generally acceptable. The following major computerized systems were used by the site: S. No. …

sections.title: Good manufacturing practices for pharmaceutical products
sections.text: Manufacturing processes were clearly defined and systematically reviewed. Qualifications/validations, calibrations, and maintenance were performed in accordance with the prepared protocols and the relevant established procedures. Manufacturing steps were recorded in batch manufacturing and packaging records. BMRs and BPRs were available during the facility tour. …

sections.title: Sanitation and hygiene
sections.text: Premises and equipment were maintained at a satisfactory level of cleanliness during the inspection. Appropriate gowning was in place for staff and visitors in all areas. The company had procedures in place for personal health and hygiene.

sections.title: Qualification and validation
sections.text: The validation master plan from corporate Cipla was reviewed. One batch every 3 years was revalidated for the product manufacturing process; one batch every year was revalidated for cleaning verification; analytical revalidation was every 7 years; and equipment/utilities requalification was every 5 years. CSVs were reviewed every 3 years before revalidation. In general, the VMP was found to be adequate in covering qualification and validation activities for personnel, facilities, change control, deviations, and risk management. …

sections.title: Complaints
sections.text: The product complaints were classified as critical, major, or minor. A process flowchart was provided in the procedure. Complaints were handled using TrackWise. For the past three years, there have been no complaints about Artesunate suppositories 100mg. No complaint was received in 2025 related to soft gelatine capsules.

sections.title: Product recalls
sections.text: The recall procedure was in place, providing instructions for the removal of product from domestic and export markets. The procedure described the classification, level, handling, and closing of recalls. Also, a mock recall procedure was delineated. No product recall related to Artesunate suppositories 100mg took place.

sections.title: Contract production, analysis and other activities
sections.text: The manufacturing activities, including the production and analysis of Artesunate Suppositories 100mg, were carried out on-site.

sections.title: Self-inspection, quality audits and suppliers’ audits and approval
sections.text: Internal audits were performed in accordance with the SOP.
